Shapoorji Pallonji Group Seeks Up to $200 Million in Private Credit to Tackle Debt Obligations

29 Oct 2026, 11:18 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.business-standard.com

Fundraising Plans and Debt Management

Indian conglomerate Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group is reportedly in early-stage talks to raise between $150 million and $200 million through private credit. According to sources familiar with the discussions, the capital is intended to address mounting debt obligations and alleviate pressure on the group's loan-to-value ratios.

The proposed financing structure involves issuing additional rupee bonds through Eqyizen Investment Pvt., an SP Group unit that previously issued similar debt in July. Approximately half of the anticipated proceeds are earmarked for repaying creditors of Porteast Investment Ltd., another subsidiary within the conglomerate. The remaining funds are slated to address other group-level debt commitments.

Because the negotiations are currently at an early stage, both the final fundraising size and the specific terms remain subject to change. Representatives for the SP Group did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the fundraising initiative.

Background and Context

The conglomerate has faced financial strain amid upcoming debt maturities and extended timelines for monetizing major assets. Among these assets is the group's substantial holding in Tata Sons Pvt., where the Mistry family—which controls the SP Group—holds an approximately 18.4 percent stake, making them the second-largest shareholder. Monetization efforts have been complicated by ongoing discussions among executives regarding whether to pursue a public listing for Tata Sons.

This latest funding push follows previous capital-raising activities. In September, the group borrowed approximately ₹4,450 crore (around $467 million) via Eqyizen and through dollar bonds issued by another unit, Mercury Finance Co. Those funds were similarly directed toward amortisation payments due at Porteast Investment.

Sources indicate that the group is aiming to complete the newly proposed financing arrangement by mid-November, though terms and timelines could shift as discussions progress.

Practical Implications and What Remains Unknown

For market observers and creditors, the ongoing efforts by the SP Group highlight the continued reliance on private credit markets to manage liquidity and service debt obligations while larger asset monetization plans remain pending.

  • What is confirmed: The SP Group is exploring a private credit raise of $150 million to $200 million via Eqyizen Investment Pvt. rupee bonds. About half of the proceeds are intended for Porteast Investment Ltd. creditors, aiming to lower the loan-to-value ratio. The target completion window is mid-November.
  • What remains unknown: Final terms, exact transaction sizes, and confirmed participation details are yet to be finalized as talks remain preliminary. Representatives for the conglomerate have not issued an official statement.
